::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** [Summer 1864][^1]  
**Manuscript:** MS location unknown. This fragment printed in <i>[Dulce Domum](other_books/otherbook_122.qmd)</i>, 175.
:::

My dear [Alice](people/person_1025.qmd),
I was thinking of sending ‘The Mice at Play’ to [Maggie](people/person_83.qmd), but somehow I felt that the note must be to one who could remember the old days, when the three bright faces[^2] it brings to mind were with us. If you had been people who shrank from such recollections instead of cherishing them, I would of course never have disinterred this old affair, but I know you will like the recurrence to those merry old days and bright remembrances.

---

[^1]: This is printed by the author of *Dulce Domum* as part of a group of fragments with dates ranging from May to October 1864.
[^2]: Two of the faces must be those of Alice’s second brother, [Arthur Moberly](people/person_1011.qmd) (1840?-1858), and second sister, [Mary Louisa (Moberly) Ridding](people/person_1020.qmd) (1838-1859). The third person was perhaps [WCY](people/person_1631.qmd).
